clues: Neither Lou nor Mabel ordered the scone.
Selma came in later than whoever took the window seat.
Either Kenji or Priya ordered the croissant.
Neither Selma nor Priya came in at 8:00 a.m.
Of Priya and the bagel customer, one came in at 8:00 a.m. and the other at 7:30 a.m.
The 8:30 a.m. customer sat neither at the counter nor on the patio.
Whoever came in at 8:30 a.m. ordered either the danish or the croissant.
Mabel ordered neither the muffin nor the bagel.
The window seat went to either Selma or Lou.
The customer in the corner seat came in half an hour after the one in the window seat.
Whoever ordered the bagel sat either in the corner or at the counter.
hints: Look at the window seat and clue 9's two choices for it. Does another clue rule one of them out?
Two clues at once: clue 2 compares Selma with the window customer. Could Selma come in later than herself?
Clue 2 keeps Selma out of the window, so by clue 9 Lou sat there. Clues 1, 3, 8 and 11 then leave Lou only the muffin.
Clues 5 and 4 put Priya at 7:30 and the bagel at 8:00. Clues 7 and 2 then leave Lou only 7:00.

solution.key_idea: Clue 2 keeps Selma out of the window seat, so clue 9 puts Lou there, right beside the corkboard.
steps: Clues 8, 1 and 3 rule out the muffin, bagel, scone and croissant for Mabel, so she ordered the danish.
Clue 2 keeps Selma out of the window seat, so by clue 9 Lou sat there. Clue 11 keeps the bagel from the window.
Lou had no scone (clue 1), croissant (clue 3), bagel or danish, so Lou had the muffin.
By clue 5, Priya came at 7:30 or 8:00, and clue 4 makes it 7:30. So by clue 5, the bagel came at 8:00.
Clues 7 and 2 keep Lou's muffin off 8:30 and 9:00, so Lou came at 7:00. By clue 4, the 8:00 bagel was Kenji's.
By clue 3, Priya had the croissant, Selma the scone. Clue 7 keeps the scone off 8:30: Selma came at 9:00, Mabel at 8:30.
By clue 10, the corner customer came in at 7:30: Priya. By clue 11, Kenji's bagel went to the counter.
Clue 6 keeps Mabel, at 8:30, off the patio, so she sat in the booth and Selma on the patio.
solution.epilogue: Lou had pocketed the card to have it framed behind glass, safe from flour and fingers, as a surprise for Rosa. It came back the next week, and Gloria looked much relieved.
